description: Deployment units and their order. The units job of mirror-deploy-unit refuses a unit that is not listed here or is listed with enabled false, and the unit of a deploy-excluded file, which is previewed and never deployed. Every other unit deploys from the pipeline, as a deployment stack named mirror-<unit>. A resource group unit is a resource group stack, a subscription unit a subscription stack and a tenant-kind unit a management group stack. A unit marked "tier": "privileged" holds the role assignments of Owner, User Access Administrator and Role Based Access Control Administrator, the custom role definitions and the pipeline identities' own roles, and deploys through the mirror-privileged-<folder> environment with that subscription's govern identity. Every other unit is production tier and deploys through mirror-production-<folder>. A tenant-kind unit names the management group it deploys against in "managementGroup". A unit with "stackDeletes": true deletes a resource that left its template when it is deployed. Without the field, or with false, the resource is detached and stays in Azure. A resource group and a management group are always detached, and stackDeletes may not be true for a tenant-kind unit or a unit of the subscription fdm-apim. A unit gets "deployed": true in a code pull request after its first deployment, and the weekly drift check then previews its stack. Paths are relative to the repository root.

allowedPrincipals.use: Interactive, reviewed runs by hand. Fill in your own sign-in name to run deploy-unit.ps1 yourself. An empty name never matches.

units.name: pilot-empty-rg
units.notes: Empty template against rg-demo-pilot, an empty resource group created by hand for the pilot alone. Proves identity, roles, the reviewers' approval and evidence capture without touching a resource.

units.name: rg-demo-network
units.notes: One network security group with no rules of its own and one virtual network with one subnet, which that network security group protects, and the private endpoint of the secrets vault with its DNS zone, link and zone group. The group's lock, policy assignment and Reader role assignment are here too. Free resources apart from the private endpoint.

units.name: rg-demo-routing
units.notes: One route table with no routes, one application security group and one Automation account with a credential whose password is read from the secrets vault with getSecret. Free resources only.

units.name: demo-subscription
units.notes: Demo subscription layer: the four resource groups rg-demo-identities, rg-demo-pilot, rg-demo-network and rg-demo-routing, written out as they are live, and the Defender plan for virtual machines. The resources inside the groups deploy from their own resource group files in resource-groups/, one unit each, and main.bicep calls none of those files. It calls the identity group's file only when deployIdentityGroup is on, which parameters.bicepparam leaves off and parameters.verify.bicepparam turns on for a preview. The Owner role assignment and the custom role of the subscription are in demo-privileged. Deployed by the pipeline through mirror-production-demo like every other unit.

units.name: demo-privileged
units.notes: The privileged part of the demo-subscription unit: the Owner role assignment on rg-demo-network, the custom role definition Demo Reader Plus, and later the standing roles of the pipeline's own identities. Only the subscription's govern identity writes them, after approval in mirror-privileged-demo. Nothing else is declared here. It runs after demo-subscription and rg-demo-network, which create the resource group the Owner assignment sits on.

units.name: demo-tenant-management-group
units.notes: The management group mg-demo, with no subscription link. It deploys at management group scope against the Tenant Root Group, which declares the child group with scope tenant(), so nothing is assigned or deployed at the root scope /. Privileged tier: the pipeline deploys it through mirror-privileged-tenant with the tenant govern identity, which holds User Access Administrator, Management Group Contributor and Mirror Deployment Operator at the Tenant Root Group. The reader previews it with Reader and Mirror What-If Reader there.

units.name: demo-tenant-governance
units.notes: One Reader role assignment made directly on the management group mg-demo. Runs after demo-tenant-management-group, which declares the group. Privileged tier: the pipeline deploys it through mirror-privileged-tenant with the tenant govern identity, at management group scope against mg-demo, as a management group stack like every other tenant unit. The reader previews it with Reader and Mirror What-If Reader at the Tenant Root Group.

units.name: rg-demo-identities-deploy-excluded
units.notes: The pipeline's own identities, their federated credentials and the secrets vault, in rg-demo-identities. The file is deploy-excluded, so this unit is previewed by pull requests and never deployed. The group is changed by hand at the setup steps. Run workflow refuses the unit.

units.name: lifecycle-proof
units.notes: A network security group, an application security group and a route table in rg-demo-lifecycle, a resource group created by hand for this unit alone. All are free. The unit shows a stack's whole life in the pipeline: a first run that only creates, an update, a resource that leaves the template and is detached, and a resource that leaves it and is deleted.
